title: Measuring Uncertainty Calibration
claim: Different smoothness assumptions on the underlying function can be sketched side by side, and ours relaxes the standard restrictive one.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, each with titled box, formula, and sketched curve
description: Three rounded-border panels sit side by side. Each has a bold title, a formula, and a hand-drawn-style curve of eta against s on simple axes. Left, Lipschitz Smoothness: the Lipschitz inequality sits above a smooth rising curve with crossing dashed lines marking the slope bound. A note says it is standard in the literature. Middle, Bounded Variation: a piecewise-constant step function with jumps labelled |Delta|. A caption says few or short jumps mean small TV, and points to section 4. Right, Bounded Derivatives: bounds on the first and second derivatives sit above a concave curve with a dashed tangent line labelled |eta'| <= b1. A note points to section 5. The figure is black and white, and the eye goes first to the bold titles and curves.
caption: Various assumptions on η(s) = E[Y | S = s].
abstract: We make two contributions to the problem of estimating the $L_1$ calibration error of a binary classifier from a finite dataset. First, we provide an upper bound for any classifier where the calibration function has bounded variation. Second, we provide a method of modifying any classifier so that its calibration error can be upper bounded efficiently without significantly impacting classifier performance and without any restrictive assumptions. All our results are non-asymptotic and distribution-free. We conclude by providing advice on how to measure calibration error in practice. Our methods yield practical procedures that can be run on real-world datasets with modest overhead.
